Settings

🎨 String colours

🥁 Drum colours

🎨 Theme

The app's colours: Dark (the default), Light, High contrast (black and white, a yellow focus ring), Midnight blue or Warm; Automatic follows your system's light or dark setting. The string colours are their own setting; on a light theme the palest are drawn darker so they read. Synced and exported with your settings.

📐 Layout

Automatic is the default. Rail (computers): a rail on the left with Songs, Play, Train, Progress and Create; Songs, Play and Create open a panel beside the tab, Train and Progress take the place of the tab. Modes (phones, tablets held upright): the same five as a tab bar at the bottom. The 📐 button in the top bar switches between them and turns Automatic off; tick Automatic again to go back to it. Kept for this device only (not in backups).

Buttons

Icons only: a calmer screen with more room; hover a button (or press and hold it on a touch screen) to see its name. The rail and the tab bar keep their words. Kept for this device only.

🎸 Chord names

The names above the tab (C, Am7, D/F#) in Scrolling, Page and Highway. All (the default): the song's own names (its chord templates, a Guitar Pro file's chord names) and, for chords without one, the names Tabloop works out from the notes sounding together (also for chords you change in ✏ Edit); one name per chord. Song's: only the song's own. Worked out: only Tabloop's. Off: none. Also the Chords menu in the view toolbar.

Names worked out for 2 notes played together (with nothing else ringing). Power chords only (the default): a 5th is the power chord on the lower note (E5), a 4th an inverted one, named by its upper note over the lower (D5/A). Power chords and double stops: 3rds and 6ths too, named as the chord they most likely belong to, in lighter italics as the chord is only implied (C + E: C, A + C: Am, C + A: Am/C, E + C: C/E). Octaves, 2nds, 7ths and the tritone are never named. A riff of the same power chord is named once (again after 4 s without a chord, or for another voicing). The note card always shows the 2-note name, whatever this is set to.

🎼 Tab

How the strings are stacked in Scrolling and Page (string names, notes, chords, ghost notes and markers, ✏ Edit) and in the 🎼 Scales fretboard. Low string on top puts the low E (the thickest string; B on a 7-string, E or B on a bass) on top, as you see the guitar when you look down at it. Bends still point up (up in pitch). The Highway keeps its lanes (the lowest string on the left, as on the neck and a chord diagram), and chord diagrams stay as usual. In ✏ Edit, Shift+↑ / ▲ moves a note to the string drawn above it.

🎵 Lyrics

For a song with lyrics that you open for the first time: the karaoke bar, the In tab row and the lyrics in the 🎤 Vocals tab. Each song then remembers its own Lyrics tick in the toolbar, whatever this is set to.

🎯 Note feedback

How the notes you play are shown on the tab, with 👂 Live and recorded takes.

Markers: 🎯 nailed (on time and in tune); a triangle where a note was off, pointing to what: ▲ sharp, ▼ flat, ◀ early, ▶ late; yellow a little off (up to twice the limit), red clearly off; ✕ missed. The limits: ±40 ms and ±15 ¢. Hover a marker for the numbers.

⚖️ How forgiving the judging is

How far off a note can be and still count as right — on time within ± ms, in tune within ± cents. One setting for 👂 Live and recorded takes: the ✓ and X/Y counts, ghost colours, markers, take summaries and timing marks all follow it, and what's shown is judged again right away.

Typing a value makes it Custom (timing 10–150 ms, pitch 5–50 ¢). Now: ±40 ms and ±15 ¢.

For when you're sure of the notes and want to work on speed and timing: a note played on time counts as right whatever its pitch — only early, late, missed and extra count (no flat or sharp). Ghost notes are coloured by timing (green on time, yellow a little off, red clearly off), markers show only 🎯 ◀ ▶ ✕, and the pitch heard is still shown on the hint card (not judged). Also the ⏱ button in the 👂 Live bar (takes follow it too: their summary then says “Timing only”). Singing below is judged on pitch by nature, so it isn't affected.

🎤 Singing (🎙 Sing in the Vocals tab) has its own, wider pitch limit: each sung note counts as in tune when the middle of it is within ± cents of the melody. Timing isn't judged for singing.

Typing a value makes it Custom (5–100 ¢). Now: ±30 ¢.

👂 Live

On by default: each song with a tab (scales and backing tracks too, not YouTube videos) starts listening as soon as it's ready, as if you pressed 👂 Live — the browser asks for the microphone the first time. Turning Live off is for that song; the next one starts it again. If the microphone is refused or missing, the message shows once and songs stop starting Live by themselves until the page is reloaded (or 👂 Live, pressed, opens the input). Untick it and 👂 Live stays as you leave it.

⏱ Calibration

Line up what you see, hear and play on this setup: the cursor against the sound (screens and Bluetooth headphones are often late), and your input's delay, used by ⏺ Rec, 👂 Live and 🎤 Sing. Then a short check, and 🎯 Target practice: play notes on clicks and see each one land on a bullseye (timing and pitch). Kept per output and input device in this browser only (never exported or synced).

Calibrate… and 🔍 Check input… are in 🎸 Tune & Input (in the top bar); 🎯 Target practice is in Progress.

🎚 Levels and the input

The song's, the tab synth's, the metronome's and My take's levels are in the 🎚 Mixer (the top bar; the parts also on Play → Tracks), remembered as you set them; the input device, its level and monitoring are in 🎸 Tune & Input.

🎸 HQ sounds

Recorded guitars, basses and drums for the tab synth's parts: clean and distorted electric guitar, nylon-string (classical) guitar, finger and picked bass, and a drum kit. On by default: they download in the background the first time a song plays with the tab synth or the MIDI drums, and are kept in this browser for offline use. Until they're there (or offline, or if the download fails) the synth plays, as it does for steel-string acoustic parts, keys and anything they don't cover. Free samples (CC0) from FreePats and Virtuosity Drums (Karoryfer): see Privacy & about.

🔄 Sync folder

Keep settings, practice history, saved loops and playlists in sync across your computers: choose a folder on this computer that Google Drive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive syncs (e.g. a “Tabloop” folder in Google Drive), then the same folder on your other computers. The app then saves to it and reads from it automatically.

💾 Export / import

Settings, per-song state and practice history are kept in this browser. Export them to back them up or to move them to another browser.

☁ Google Drive

Optional: back up settings and practice history to your own Google Drive, in a private app folder only this app can see. With several computers, each compares itself with the backup when it starts and asks if both changed.

⭐ Premium

Most of Tabloop is free, and every tool below has a free taste; premium unlocks all of it. Locked controls show a 🔒 and stay visible, so you can see what they do. Your practice is always recorded in full.

    ▶ Open a YouTube video

    Paste a YouTube link or a video id. The video plays in YouTube's own player; Tabloop drives it: ▶ / ❚❚, the seek bar, A/B loops, sections you mark, saved loops and the speed.

    Not for YouTube videos: pitch, ⏺ Rec, 👂 Live and the mixer (the sound stays inside YouTube's player). A tab part can be added from a picture of a tab (📷 Tab from an image). Speed: the steps the video offers (usually 25–200 %).

    This copy of Tabloop was opened from a file: YouTube usually refuses to play videos in it. Use the online version, tabloop.github.io.

    By playing YouTube videos you agree to the YouTube Terms of Service; Google's Privacy Policy applies. Opening a video loads YouTube's player (youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com): see the privacy policy. Spotify isn't supported (why).

    ＋ Create a song

    Your own recording and a tab for it: line them up (⇆ Sync), then 💾 Save pack makes a feedpak. Or a new empty song, written from scratch in ✏ Edit or by playing it (⏺ Transcribe). Everything is read and kept on this device; nothing is uploaded.

    1 · The recording

    MP3, M4A (AAC), WAV, OGG, FLAC or Opus, as your browser plays them. Or drop it on this window, or open it with Open file.

    📷 Tab from an image

    A picture of a tab — a photo of a tab book or sheet, an image file, a screenshot you've taken: paste it here (⌘V / Ctrl+V), drop it, or choose the file. It's read on this device, never uploaded, and not kept: only the notes are saved, as a tab part of this song.
